fieldValues.title: Federation returns, starting with cross-repository addressing
fieldValues.decision_question: Is federation's committed return (decision 4f1e12e5) scheduled now, and in what order?
fieldValues.context: Owner, 2026-10-16: essays will live in their own repository and link into muSrs and other repositories within a federation; the MCP server should address several repositories, tested and managed. This is the trigger 4f1e12e5 first named (a second real repository needing live cross-repository assertions); its return is committed and the owner schedules it. RFC-049 (Draft Rev 3, srs#913) already specifies addressing (Address.repositoryId, a boundary directory, read-only resolution) and states that accepting it is the scheduling act. Problems SP-86 and SP-87 recorded the same day.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: Keep essays in muSrs and defer federation (no spec change; muSrs keeps growing). Copy linked records into each essay repository (duplicates that drift; SP-34). Implement multi-repo MCP ahead of the spec (an implementation leading the spec, against the charter).
fieldValues.decision_statement: Federation's return is scheduled now, in three steps: (1) take RFC-049 through review to acceptance (cross-repository addressing and read-only resolution); (2) a follow-up RFC for cross-repository relations, so a record in one repository can link to a record in another; (3) multi-repository MCP serving (srs-rust#683) implementing (1), with conformance tests. Until (2) lands, essays stay in muSrs.
fieldValues.rationale: The need is real and named by the owner, the design is half written (RFC-049), and the charter requires the spec to lead the implementation; addressing first keeps each step small and reversible.
fieldValues.revisit_when: RFC-049 is rejected or reworked, or essays stop needing records outside their own repository.
